It rewards players who love initiative and clear attacking plans. €69.90 China take down Armenia China strengthened their position at the top of the Women's Chess Olympiad in round nine, defeating Armenia 3–1 to move two match points clear of their nearest rivals with only two rounds remaining. The fourth seeds are now on 17/18 match points, having won eight matches and drawn one. India, Kazakhstan and Mongolia form the closest chasing group on 15/18, while six more teams stand another point back on 14/18. China's win over Armenia came through victories on boards one and three. Zhu Jiner defeated Lilit Mkrtchian, while Lu Miaoyi beat Elina Danielian. Song Yuxin and Zhai Mo drew their games, leaving China with a clear 3–1 result. The pairing carried some extra significance after Armenia had beaten China at the 2024 Olympiad, with Zhu and Lu both losing in that match. This time, the two Chinese players reversed those individual outcomes and helped their team consolidate first place. Zhu has also continued a strong individual event and remains one of China's most reliable scorers. India close the gap with a clear win India responded well after drawing former co-leaders Kazakhstan in round eight, defeating hosts Uzbekistan 3–1. The decisive points came from Divya Deshmukh and Vantika Agrawal. Divya defeated Gulrukhbegim Tokhirjonova on board two, while Vantika beat Nilufarkhon Imomkuzieva on board three. Humpy Koneru and Savitha Shri drew their games - this was Savitha's first draw in the event, as she started with an astounding 7 wins from 7 games. The result lifted the defending champions to 15/18 and second place on tiebreaks. Deshmukh and Vantika both remain unbeaten in Samarkand, and their wins ensured that India will enter the penultimate round with a direct chance to challenge the leaders. That opportunity comes immediately: China and India will face each other in round ten on Saturday. With a two-point gap between them, the result of that match will have a major effect on the final standings. Kazakhstan recover to hold Mongolia Bibisara Assaubayeva | Photo: Michal Walusza / FIDE Third seeds Kazakhstan also reached 15/18, but only after recovering from a difficult start against Mongolia. Mongolia took a 2–0 lead on the lower boards, with Khishigbaatar Bayasgalan defeating Meruert Kamalidenova and Batkhuyag Munguntuul beating Zarina Nurgaliyeva. Kazakhstan then struck back on the top two boards: Bibisara Assaubayeva defeated Bat-Erdene Mungunzul, while Alua Nurman beat Turmunkh Munkhzul to salvage a 2–2 draw. Bat-Erdene Mungunzul on board one | Photo: Michal Walusza / FIDE Nurman's result was particularly important, as it prevented Mongolia from moving to within one point of China. Kazakhstan remain unbeaten as a team after nine rounds, with six wins and three draws. Mongolia, seeded 15 th , nevertheless continue to be one of the notable performers of the tournament. Their 15/18 score leaves them level with India and Kazakhstan and very much in contention heading into the final weekend. Six teams follow on 14/18 France, Armenia, Poland, Vietnam, Indonesia and Greece make up the next group on 14/18. France edged Serbia 2½–1½ in a match featuring three decisive games. Deimante Daulyte-Cornette and Pauline Guichard scored the French wins, while Sofia Pogorelskikh replied for Serbia. Poland also won by the narrowest margin, beating Cuba 2½–1½. Oliwia Kiolbasa and Klaudia Kulon scored victories for Poland, while Ineymig Hernandez Gil won for Cuba. Vietnam produced one of the clearest results among the chasing teams, defeating Bulgaria 3½–½. Wins for Thi Kim Phung Vo, Ngoc Thuy Duong Bach and Thi Mai Hung Nguyen lifted the 21st seeds into the group on 14 points. Indonesia also reached 14/18 with a notable 2½–1½ victory over Germany, while Greece held second-seeded Georgia to a 2–2 draw. China and India meet in penultimate round Saturday's tenth round will bring the most important pairing of the women's event so far, with China facing India. A Chinese victory would give them a four-point advantage with only one round remaining, while an Indian win would bring the defending champions level on match points before the final round. Kazakhstan will face France, Mongolia will meet Poland, Armenia will play Greece, while Vietnam and Indonesia - two of the lower-seeded teams still in the leading group - will face each other. With two rounds to go, China have created the clearest lead seen so far in the women's section, but India, Kazakhstan and Mongolia remain close enough to keep the race open.
